expect:
Students may include two of the following points, but all other relevant points must be credited:
• Christianity teaches that forgiveness is essential — Jesus said 'If you forgive other people when they sin against you, your heavenly Father will also forgive you' (Matthew 6:14). Forgiveness is a duty for Christians.
• Similarly, Islam teaches that forgiveness brings reward from Allah — 'Whoever pardons and makes reconciliation, his reward is with Allah' (Qur'an 42:40). Muslims are encouraged to forgive because Allah is 'the most forgiving'.
• Both religions teach that forgiveness can lead to reconciliation and the restoration of relationships.

Students may include two of the following points, but all other relevant points must be credited:
• Christianity — many Christians believe violence is always wrong because Jesus said 'If anyone strikes you on the right cheek, turn the other also' (Matthew 5:39). Quakers follow this teaching literally and reject every form of violence.
• Islam — most Muslims believe violence is allowed in self-defence because the Qur'an says 'Those who have been attacked are permitted to take up arms' (22:39). The lesser jihad permits armed struggle, but only under strict conditions such as legitimate authority, proportion and last resort.
• Some Christians also accept that violence can be a last resort once every peaceful option has failed, because they believe protecting innocent life is a duty.
Students must refer to Christianity and at least one other tradition.
[4 marks]

In your answer you should refer to the main religious tradition of Great Britain and one or more other religious traditions.

Explain two contrasting religious beliefs in contemporary British society about pacifism.
In your answer you should refer to the main religious tradition of Great Britain and one or more other religious traditions.

expect:
1 mark per simple point, 2 marks per developed point (maximum 4 marks). If the two beliefs are not contrasting, maximum 2 marks.
• Some Christians, such as Quakers, believe all conflict should be resolved peacefully. Jesus said ‘Blessed are the peacemakers’ (Matthew 5:9), meaning those who work for peace are closest to God. They refused to fight in wars but served as mediators and medics instead.
• Some Muslims believe that while peace is preferred, sometimes fighting is necessary to establish peace. The Qur’an permits self-defence (‘Those who have been attacked are permitted to take up arms’) but also teaches ‘if they incline towards peace, you must also incline towards it’ (Qur’an 8:61).
value:
1 mark per simple point, 2 marks per developed point (maximum 4 marks). Each belief needs a reason. If the two beliefs are not contrasting, maximum 2 marks.
• Some Christians are absolute pacifists. Quakers refused to fight in the First and Second World Wars because Jesus said ‘Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God’ (Matthew 5:9). They served as mediators, medics, cooks and mechanics instead.
• Most Muslims are not absolute pacifists. They believe fighting can be necessary, because the Prophet Muhammad spoke of a lesser jihad as well as the greater jihad. Peace is still preferred: the Qur’an teaches ‘Making peace is better’ (Surah 4:128) and ‘if they incline towards peace, you must also incline towards it’ (Qur’an 8:61).
• Some Christians reject absolute pacifism, arguing that refusing to fight can leave innocent people unprotected.
Students must refer to Christianity and at least one other tradition.
